question: What is the main goal of the Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) model in health facilities?

options.A: Providing free medications to all citizens
options.B: Generating high profits for hospital management
options.C: Ensuring continuous availability of essential medicines
options.D: Reducing the salary burden of pharmacy staff

explanation: The core purpose of the DRF is to maintain a constant stock of drugs by recycling funds generated from patient sales back into buying new stock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h1)

question: A primary health centre runs out of cash to buy new drugs because many patients received medications on credit. This breaks which core rule of the DRF model?

options.A: Cash generated must be strictly reinvested into fresh stock procurement
options.B: Government subventions must cover all operational losses
options.C: Medicines must be sold at manufacturing cost without any addition
options.D: Staff salaries must be deducted directly from the drug sales account

explanation: The revolving system fails when cash is tied up in credit or used elsewhere, leaving no money to buy replacement drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h1)

question: Electricity bills used to power the vaccine refrigerator in a hospital pharmacy are an example of what type of cost?
explanation: Overhead expenses like electricity for storage and keeping vaccines cold are classified as indirect operational costs. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why must pharmacy managers calculate both direct and indirect costs when pricing DRF medicines?

options.A: To ensure the selling price fully covers all operational expenses for sustainability
options.B: To comply with international tax laws on imported pharmaceuticals
options.C: To determine the exact salary scale of the pharmacy technicians
options.D: To prove to the government that no profits are being generated

explanation: Ignoring indirect costs causes the fund to slowly deplete because overhead expenses eat into the core capital. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h2)

question: Transport fees paid when moving drugs from a central port to a zonal medical store are classified as what?
explanation: Movement of goods and transport fees form part of the procurement logistics expenses added to the supply chain. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h3)

question: What happens to a DRF stock if transport and clearing expenses are consistently left out of the pricing formula?

options.A: Suppliers will offer lower invoice prices to compensate
options.B: The capital base shrinks over time, leading to stockouts
options.C: Patients will buy more drugs due to cheaper prices
options.D: The fund automatically receives emergency grants from donors

explanation: Absorbing unbudgeted transport costs out of pocket exhausts the fund's capital, making it impossible to fully replace stock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of adding a sustainability mark-up to DRF drugs?

options.A: To pay the personal medical bills of all hospital staff
options.B: To increase the basic salary of the chief medical director
options.C: To generate heavy profits for private pharmaceutical investors
options.D: To absorb losses from inflation, wastage, and operational overheads

explanation: The sustainability margin protects the fund against losses like expired drugs, damaged items, and rising prices. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h4)

question: A hospital pharmacy manager sets the DRF drug mark-up to zero percent to make medicines free. What happens next?

options.A: Suppliers will begin providing subsequent drug batches free of charge
options.B: The fund will collapse completely once the initial stock gets exhausted
options.C: Patients will donate money voluntarily to keep the shelves filled
options.D: The federal government will automatically refund the exact total purchase cost

explanation: Without a mark-up to cover extra expenses and inflation, the revolving fund cannot buy replacement stock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h4)

question: How can a pharmacy maintain fairness in a DRF while still protecting overall fund capital?

options.A: Applying lower mark-ups on essential chronic disease drugs and balancing with other items
options.B: Selling all medications strictly below the original manufacturer purchase price
options.C: Charging double prices for emergency drugs used by wealthy individuals
options.D: Stopping the purchase of expensive medicines for poor patients entirely

explanation: Balancing prices across different drugs allows vulnerable patients to afford critical medicines without ruining the fund financially. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which pricing approach is NOT recommended for ensuring fairness within a public sector DRF?

options.A: Protecting chronic disease drugs from aggressive inflation hikes
options.B: Using a flat sustainable mark-up on fast-moving consumables
options.C: Charging exorbitant mark-ups exclusively on emergency antibiotics

explanation: Putting heavy mark-ups on critical emergency drugs harms vulnerable patients and defeats the public health goal of fairness. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the main impact of local currency devaluation on a drug revolving fund that imports medications?

options.A: It reduces the total number of patients visiting the clinic
options.B: It eliminates all indirect operational expenses in the pharmacy
options.C: It automatically lowers the shipping costs of pharmaceutical goods
options.D: It increases the replacement cost of future drug procurements

explanation: When local currency drops in value, buying foreign drugs becomes more expensive, requiring more money to get the same amount of stock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is signing a long-term fixed price supply contract risky for a DRF during high inflation?

options.A: The pharmacy will make too much profit from unsuspecting patients
options.B: Suppliers may default or abandon contracts when market prices outpace the agreed rate
options.C: Government auditors will ban the pharmacy from buying local brands
options.D: Patients will refuse to buy drugs priced below the inflation rate

explanation: When inflation surges, fixed-price contracts become unprofitable for manufacturers, leading them to abandon supplies and leave shelves empty. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which inventory control method groups drugs based on their annual consumption value to prioritize management?
explanation: ABC analysis helps managers focus tight financial control on high-value items that take up most of the DRF budget. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why are routine physical stock counts essential for sustaining a hospital drug revolving fund?

options.A: To prove to pharmaceutical manufacturers that the hospital is wealthy
options.B: To reconcile ledger records with actual inventory and detect pilferage or losses
options.C: To calculate the annual Christmas bonus for the pharmacy staff
options.D: To ensure that expired drugs are immediately sold off to patients at a discount

explanation: Physical audits expose issues like missing stock, counting errors, or unrecorded debts before they crash the fund. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h7)
